Senses.Explanation: Literally, a straight or straightforward mind. The term occurs 163 times in 89 allowed texts. The corpus supplies two compact definitions: 'straight mind means without bends or twists' (直心者，無委曲故), and 'straight mind is the site of the Way because it has no falseness' (直心是道場，無虛假故). The Platform Record repeats 'straight mind is the site; straight mind is the clean land' (直心是道場，直心是淨土), then contrasts inwardly acting crookedly while verbally speaking straight with actually carrying out straight mind. Its positive clause is 'only carry out straight mind; regarding all things, have no grasping' (但行直心，於一切法上，無有執著). Another address expands the pattern into four coordinated expressions: 'straight mind is the site; straight speech is the subtle teaching; straight conduct is subtle conduct; straight verification is the subtle result' (直心是道場，直說是妙法，直行是妙行，直證是妙果). The common collocation 'straight mind and straight conduct' (直心直行) occurs 22 times in 16 texts. One record describes it by the absence of self-versus-other, right-versus-wrong, falseness, and crookedness; another uses 'straight mind, straight conduct, original color, original share' (直心直行，本色本分) to characterize a master's meetings with people.
Senses.Note: The English follows the graph meaning 'straight' (直) and the texts' own oppositions: straight versus crooked (直／曲), genuine versus false (真實／虛假), and straight conduct versus flattering crookedness (諂曲). The direct definition 'without bends or twists' occurs once, while the site-of-the-Way formula occurs across multiple independent records. No master-specific sense is warranted.

Senses.PreferredTarget: directly pointing at the human mind
AlternateTargets: pointing straight at the person's mind
Senses.Explanation: (直) = directly/straight, (指) = point, (人心) = the person's mind. One of the four stock phrases the corpus attaches to Bodhidharma's coming from the West, paired with (見性成佛) ('see nature, become Buddha') in 470 of its 624 allowlist hits (190 files) and preceded by (不立文字) ('not setting up words') in 118 (79 files). Attested deployment: (a) the slogan of what Bodhidharma brought -- (達磨西來不立文字)。(直指人心見性成佛) ('Bodhidharma came from the West not setting up words -- directly pointing at the human mind, seeing nature and becoming Buddha'; Dahui, T47n1997); (達磨西來直指人心見性成佛)。(亦復如是) ('Bodhidharma came from the West directly pointing at the human mind, seeing nature and becoming Buddha; and so it is likewise'; Huitang Zuxin, T51n2077); the Blue Cliff Record (碧巖錄) variant carries (單傳心印) ('the single transmission of the mind-seal') alongside it (謂之教外別傳。單傳心印。直指人心。見性成佛 -- 'this is called a separate transmission outside the teachings, the single transmission of the mind-seal, directly pointing at the human mind, seeing nature and becoming Buddha'; T48n2003); (b) a gloss in a master's own words -- Dahui: (達磨西來不立文字語句)。(唯直指人心)。(若論直指)。(只人人本有) ('Bodhidharma came from the West setting up no words or phrases -- only directly pointing at the human mind; as for direct pointing, just what every person inherently has', T47n1997); (c) a test-question -- (如何是直指人心) ('what is directly pointing at the human mind?'; 4 hits / 4 files), with the recorded answers (舌在口裏) ('the tongue is in the mouth'; the follow-up 如何是見性成佛？師曰：金屑雖貴，落眼成翳 -- 'what is seeing nature and becoming Buddha? The master said: gold dust, though precious, once fallen in the eye becomes a cataract', X82n1571) and (腳跟下分明看取) ('look clearly right under your heels'; answering 如何是直指人心、見性成佛之旨 -- 'what is the purport of directly pointing at the human mind, seeing nature and becoming Buddha?', J34nB311). Collocations: (單傳直指) ('single transmission, direct pointing'; 119 hits / 73 files), (直指單傳) ('direct pointing, single transmission'; 95 / 71), (西來直指) ('the direct pointing of the coming from the West'; 42 / 34), (直指之道) ('the way of direct pointing'; 67 / 34), (若論直指) ('as for direct pointing'; 13 / 13). Beyond recorded lines such as Dahui's (只人人本有) ('just what every person inherently has'), the texts leave the phrase without gloss, and so does this entry.
Senses.Note: 624 hits across 216 files of the 462-file allowlist (XML tags/notes/rdg stripped, whitespace collapsed, punctuation retained -- all counts in this entry use this convention; 見性成佛 ('seeing nature, becoming Buddha') counted as following across at most one punctuation mark). Nearly always in the Bodhidharma four-phrase frame (with 'not setting up words' (不立文字) / 'a separate transmission outside the teachings' (教外別傳) / 'seeing nature, becoming Buddha' (見性成佛)); the paired (見性成佛) is its near-constant companion (470 of 624 hits). Curated occurrences span a master's (語錄) ('recorded sayings'; Dahui), a (古尊宿) ('Ancient Worthies') anthology, a (燈錄) ('lamp record'; the 續傳燈錄, Continued Lamp Record), and the (碧巖錄) (the Blue Cliff Record, T48n2003 -- a 頌古/評唱 collection of verse-comments on old cases and prose expositions, a case-commentary collection, not a lamp record).

Senses.PreferredTarget: turn the light around and shine back
AlternateTargets: turn the light back and illuminate
turn illumination around and shine back
Senses.Explanation: Literally, 'turn the light around and shine back': 'turn around' (迴), 'light' (光), 'return' (返), and 'shine or illuminate' (照). This written form occurs 50 times in 35 allowed texts; the common variant 'turn the light around and shine back' (回光返照) occurs 168 times in 88 texts, and the reversed order 'shine back and turn the light' (返照回光) occurs 16 times. The Record of the Transmission of the Lamp gives the literal instruction, 'turn the light around and shine back; look: what are body and mind?' (迴光返照看身心是何物). Shitou's Grass Hut Song says, 'turn the light around and shine back, then return' (迴光返照便歸來). Linji tells his listeners that at the words they should 'themselves turn the light around and shine back, seeking nothing else' (便自迴光返照，更不別求). Chengtian Cique says, 'only turn the light around and shine back; carefully search beneath your own heels and look what it is' (但自迴光返照，向自己脚根下子細推尋，看是箇什麼). Gongchen Jueke closes an address with 'each of you, please turn the light around and shine back; do not hesitate further' (各請迴光返照，休更踟躕). Fenyang's verse supplies a result-clause: 'turn the light around and shine back, illuminating present and past' (迴光返照明今古). The corpus thus records an imperative verb phrase, a poetic return, a prohibition on seeking elsewhere, and direct objects or complements such as body and mind, beneath one's heels, and present and past.
Senses.Note: No required direct-definition formula was found. The entry translates the four graphs and the actions explicitly attached to them. It does not rename those instructions as a special exercise or import an external system. The common orthographic variant is recorded in the explanation, while the assigned headword and all curated anchors retain the assigned written form.
